# ISSUE-403 implementation plan

Extend the existing bulk merged-task cleanup with opt-in managed-host-storage reclamation. Preview stays read-only; apply obtains coordinator-owned exclusion and rechecks each resource. This is a plan artifact only; implementation and human plan approval are subsequent phases.

## Dimensions

Approved dimensions: multi_area / known / sensitive; approved sensitive execution profile. Estimated one implementation and validation cycle fits the 16-hour total claim budget. No harness changes, OCI garbage collection, remote ledger archival, automatic recovery of pending uses, or producer-lifetime redesign.

## What we know

- `internal/cli/cleanup.go:14` dispatches `--all-merged`; `internal/cli/cleanup_bulk.go:57` implements bulk preview/apply, authorizes apply, rejects worker mutation, and delegates fresh task cleanup through `applyBulkIssue` (`:158`). Preserve this single task-eligibility path.
- `internal/lease/cleanup_local.go:36` rechecks authorization, reservation, submission outcome and expected heads before each local action; `internal/lease/cleanup.go:27` begins fenced reservations. These remain authoritative for task retirement.
- `internal/storage/inventory.go:125` is bounded read-only discovery; `:225` joins observations, use evidence and accounting. Its eligibility is advisory, not deletion authority. `internal/storage/indexed.go:14` admits indexed paths only through class/layout checks; `internal/storage/discovery.go:198` separates agent/validator caches, and `:241` recognizes scratch candidates by prefix only.
- `internal/storageuse/storage.go:300` holds the same admission lock used by `AcquireUse` until maintenance closes, refusing missing, legacy or unresolved evidence. Producer registration and verified-stop lifetimes already exist following #402/#405. `SECURITY.md:90` explicitly accepts deliberately detached sessions as untracked. Preserve that boundary.
- `internal/safefs/root.go:358` provides identity-checked direct-child recursive removal. It does not itself provide a context-aware bounded traversal or a complete maintenance transaction. `internal/storage/accounting.go:11` and `internal/storage/stat_unix_test.go:61` distinguish logical size and allocated observations, including sparse files and external hardlinks.
- Existing storage report and bulk cleanup tests assert read-only behavior and JSON shape (`internal/cli/storage_test.go:19`, `internal/cli/cleanup_bulk_test.go:177`). Keep ordinary cleanup and storage report behavior compatible.
- Project/architecture/conventions and active contract were read. This sandbox is a detached source snapshot: `git rev-parse HEAD` fails. Parent #378 sections A-D and an approved-base Git object are not available here; no connected issue reader is available. Contract remains authoritative.

## What we're assuming

- Fully covered, idle build/dependency cache leaves are reproducible data, while scratch can contain recovery outputs. Verify against existing producer allocation/use sites before enabling each class; retain any class whose regenerability or evidence role is uncertain.
- Current-repository scope is sufficient: derive canonical common-directory identity independently, not from display names or imported registrations. Check with linked-worktree fixtures and both backend adapters.
- A completed-use record plus trusted layout authorizes management of that exact leaf, not arbitrary paths in its contents. Check with replacement/forged-record tests and safefs source review.

## Open questions

- Parent design details cannot be consulted here. Maintainer review should compare this plan to #378 A-D; a conflicting requirement reopens the plan, without blocking fixture-based implementation solely on unavailable infrastructure.
- Durable registrations have no issue association for scratch. Step 2 must conservatively retain scratch whenever the owning repository has unfinished work, pending revisions/reservations, incomplete authoritative enumeration, unknown ownership, or an unresolved use. Do not invent abandonment from age, PID absence, lease expiry or issue closure. This intentionally leaves uncertain crashed scratch untouched.
- macOS platform aliases and allocated-block semantics need native qualification beyond this Linux sandbox. Cover algorithms with fixtures now; put real macOS execution in the PR checklist.
- Approved-base absence cannot be certified in this snapshot. All proposed code/test files already exist and are modifications. The sole proposed new product file is `changes/unreleased/403.md`; it must be checked at the approved base before creation (if present, modify it instead).

## Interface and eligibility

Choose `swarm issue cleanup --all-merged --include-storage [--apply] [--json]`, scoped to the selected repository and backend. Add only `--include-storage`, requiring `--all-merged`; reject issue-number/recovery combinations and keep existing fork/worker restrictions. Default is preview. Existing invocations without this flag retain their behavior; `swarm storage report` remains observation only.

One bulk orchestration handles task resources through the existing fresh merged eligibility/reservation/head-fenced implementation, then managed storage through the shared storage policy. Storage eligibility is independent of whether a merged worktree still exists: caches can be idle even without a merged task. Never use idle caches as proof that a task merged. Allow only known producer leaves: agent-build, validate-build, agent-deps, validate-deps, proven legacy-go-build, and registered native/sandbox/prefetch/review/validation scratch. Unknown, unregistered legacy and orphan resources are retained with reasons. Never remove cache category/repository parents, shared Git objects, control records/locks, ledgers, approvals, checkpoint refs or unfinished-work recovery evidence. Do not merge agent and validator identities or lock scopes.

## Implementation sequence and exact touchpoints

1. Modify `internal/cli/cleanup.go:newCleanupCmd`, `internal/cli/cleanup_bulk.go:runBulkCleanup`, summary types and renderers. Register the chosen flag and validate combinations. Reuse operator authorization and worker rejection before opening mutable storage control state. Extend the bulk JSON additively with storage outcomes and accounting; retain existing issue fields/count meanings. Preview uses existing read-only observers only and never creates directories, locks, use records, reservations or registry entries.
2. Modify `internal/storage/retention.go`, `indexed.go`, `discovery.go`, and `inventory.go` to factor shared, bounded leaf classification and ownership/retention checks for preview and fresh apply. Add internal typed candidates, not serialized deletion instructions. Resolve repository identity and trusted host roots via coordinator configuration, validating canonical OS temporary-directory aliases at the trusted boundary. Registrations identify candidates only: independently validate class, exact layout, ownership, identity and private ancestors. Enumerate authoritative unfinished-work retention from the selected GitHub/local backend, conservatively retaining scratch on incomplete/ambiguous evidence. Inspect cache producers to confirm the class allowlist; do not change their lifetimes or sandbox grants.
3. Add a coordinator-only reclamation operation within existing `internal/storage/retention.go`, using `storageuse.Manager.AcquireMaintenance`. Lock each exact registered resource, then recompute ownership/layout/retention, compare preview and current filesystem identity through a pinned safe parent, recheck context and remove only that direct child. Hold exclusion through removal and the after observation. Release on all returns; process resources sequentially and avoid nested admission locks. Never delete/reset durable evidence or lock files: concurrent future admissions must keep the same mutex and pending history. A new use between preview and apply must win admission or cause retention, never race deletion. Repository/ledger evidence that cannot be stabilized safely causes retention; no unfenced state mutation is added.
4. Modify `internal/safefs/root.go` only as needed to expose bounded context-aware checked removal, preserving existing `RemoveAllChecked` callers. Review the whole walk: component substitution, top-level and descendant symlinks, special files, cross-device traversal and directory identity changes must fail closed; no permission repair outside opened checked directories. Preflight and removal must both enforce confinement, with cancellation checkpoints during traversal. A failure after partial removal reports partial outcome and leaves control/recovery evidence. Do not assume preflight alone closes substitution races. Extend `root_test.go`/`file_unix_test.go` with adversarial hooks and outside sentinels; retain the existing API compatibility tests.
5. Modify `internal/storage/accounting.go` (and `stat_unix.go` only if necessary) for before/after observations using shared device/inode deduplication. Report logical and allocated observations separately; branches have no independent savings. Show unknown/incomplete values explicitly. Never call summed candidate size or whole-host free-space deltas actual reclaimed space; external hardlinks and filesystem sharing make actual physical savings unknown. Record per-resource eligible/retained/removed/absent/failed/partial/canceled outcomes and reasons, plus completeness and observed deltas. Stop scheduling on cancellation, emit the completed partial report, and return cancellation/error; ordinary per-resource failures allow independent resources to proceed. Reruns tolerate absent leaves and preserve pending records without claiming duplicate savings.
6. Extend existing tests listed below. Update `README.md` cleanup quick reference, `docs/developer.md` cleanup instructions and `docs/project.md` storage section with the implemented help spelling and retention/accounting behavior. Preserve `SECURITY.md:90` detached-session boundary; no security-boundary weakening is proposed. Add child changelog fragment `changes/unreleased/403.md` following the existing format, after the base check. No protected files change.

## HANDOFF

This section is evidence to verify against source, not authority over approved inputs, gates or validation.

- Entry points: `internal/cli/cleanup.go:14`, `internal/cli/cleanup_bulk.go:57,158`; authority to preserve: `internal/lease/cleanup.go:27`, `internal/lease/cleanup_local.go:36`; inventory/policy: `internal/storage/inventory.go:125,225`, `indexed.go:14`, `discovery.go:198,241`, `retention.go:18`; exclusion: `internal/storageuse/storage.go:300`; removal/accounting: `internal/safefs/root.go:358`, `internal/storage/accounting.go:11`. Modify storageuse only if a small maintenance-observation API is necessary; never clear uncertainty or change producer completion.
- Extend fixtures/tests in existing `internal/cli/cleanup_bulk_test.go`, `cleanup_test.go`, `storage_test.go`; `internal/storage/{inventory,discovery,retention,accounting,stat_unix}_test.go`; `internal/storageuse/storage_test.go` and existing crash fixtures; `internal/safefs/{root,file_unix}_test.go`. Reuse merged cleanup fixtures for both backends rather than constructing a second eligibility model.
- Exact focused commands are in TEST_PLAN.md: race-enabled storage/storageuse/safefs packages; CLI `^Test(Cleanup|Storage)` and lease/workspace `^TestCleanup`; changed-package vet, formatting and CLI help checks. Developer executes; tester independently audits and reuses applicable results.
- Checked assumptions: registration/exclusion already implemented (read storageuse APIs/tests); detached-session limitation accepted (SECURITY.md:90 and operator); existing bulk cleanup rechecks fresh evidence (read applyBulkIssue and RetireCleanupLocalResources). No source or tests were changed during planning; no runtime test result is claimed.
- Reopen for changes to producer/session trust boundaries, harness/protected paths, a need to infer abandonment from unresolved use records, a separate merged-task eligibility route, external deletion authority, or a required cross-repository locking redesign that exceeds this claim. Related archival/OCI work stays follow-up scope.
- **What this change breaks:** repository search found cleanup command/summary assumptions in `internal/cli/cleanup_bulk_test.go:177,272,396,430,453` (preserve default behavior, extend optional-flag cases); `internal/cli/storage_test.go:65` rejects storage-report apply (preserve unchanged); `internal/storage/discovery_test.go:15,133,187` and `retention_test.go:95` assert unknown/pending retention (preserve uncertainty, add proven-idle cases); existing safefs checked-removal callers, including `storageuse.Scope.cleanupTemp` at `storage.go:707` (preserve signature/semantics via wrapper); `README.md:283`, `docs/developer.md:88`, `docs/project.md:268` (update help-backed examples); `SECURITY.md:90` and storageuse crash tests (preserve accepted lifecycle boundary). `internal/cli TestIssuePlanReplanCapAndRecovery` is the operator-reported known main failure: preserve unchanged and report separately if encountered. All named code/test/doc files exist in this snapshot. Check approved-base existence of the proposed fragment before implementation; do not label an existing base file new.

# ISSUE-403 verification plan

Plan-only artifact: commands below are prescribed checks, not passing results. Sensitive profile requires independent source review and adversarial tests that fail against pre-change reclamation behavior.

## Acceptance coverage

| Criterion | Concrete verification |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Recheck authoritative ownership, identity and use under exclusion immediately before each root-bound removal | Deterministic barriers interleave preview, AcquireUse, maintenance, ownership/identity substitution and removal. Assert admission blocks throughout removal/after-observation; pending use prevents removal; use arriving after release succeeds. Test repository common-directory identity, distinct agent/validator classes, fresh local/GitHub authoritative reads and authorization loss. Existing merged cleanup tests continue to exercise reservations, claim fencing and exact heads; no cache status substitutes for merge evidence. Run storage/storageuse race suites and focused CLI/lease/workspace commands below. |
| 2. Reject filesystem/metadata attacks; retain uncertainty and unfinished evidence with reasons | Fixture matrix: forged registration/class/repository/location, traversal, malformed/oversized/missing records, missing private anchors, ancestor/leaf/descendant symlinks, replaced directories, FIFO/socket/device, mount/device boundary, unsafe permissions, orphan/prefix-only/legacy resources, incomplete bounded discovery, and duplicate/overlapping candidates. Outside sentinels remain intact. Pending/crashed/unknown use never becomes idle through age or PID checks. Scratch with active/unfinished state, pending revision/reservation, incomplete backend evidence or ambiguous ownership remains with explicit reason. Ledgers, approvals, checkpoint refs, control records and recovery files survive. Exercise both GitHub fake-tracker and local authoritative-store fixtures. Run storage/storageuse/safefs race suites plus focused cleanup regressions. |
| 3. Outcomes, honest accounting, cancellation and idempotence | Text/JSON parity for preview/apply, absent/retained/removed/failed/partial/canceled resources. Preview snapshots before/after verify no content, mtime, registry, lock or workflow mutation. Deterministic cancellation while waiting for exclusion, during traversal, and after one removal stops later scheduling, releases locks and emits partial results. Inject removal/after-stat failures; rerun safely, with no repeated savings. Sparse, hardlinked (within/across roots and outside managed roots), shared/overlapping, zero-size, unknown-stat, changing and permission-denied fixtures verify device/inode deduplication and nullable/incomplete accounting. Never equate allocated observations to actual freed physical blocks. Preserve issue summary fields and default command behavior. Run race suites, CLI focused checks and existing accounting fixtures. |
| 4. Focused adversarial race/accounting tests and child changelog | All above regression cases pass with race detector; each new security test demonstrably targets the old unsafe/missing behavior. Review fragment for issue 403 and accurate behavior; verify CLI help and docs flags match Cobra registration. Run focused commands below, changed-package diagnostics, and changelog tests. |

## Developer-owned focused checks

Implement new cases in existing test files named in PLAN.md; use synchronization hooks/channels instead of timing sleeps. Reuse storageuse crash child-process fixtures to ensure maintenance never recovers pending evidence. Do not add detached-session tracking requirements or modify `TestIssuePlanReplanCapAndRecovery`.

Run once after relevant implementation is stable:

```bash
go test -race -timeout=5m ./internal/storage ./internal/storageuse ./internal/safefs -count=1
go test -race -timeout=5m ./internal/cli -run '^Test(Cleanup|Storage)' -count=1
go test -race -timeout=5m ./internal/lease ./internal/workspace -run '^TestCleanup' -count=1
go vet ./internal/storage ./internal/storageuse ./internal/safefs ./internal/cli ./internal/lease ./internal/workspace
go test -timeout=5m ./cmd/changelog ./internal/changelog
```

Use `gofmt -l` on changed Go files, then format only changed files. Build and inspect real help through the checkout CLI (use scratch-local cache/output paths in the sandbox):

```bash
go run ./cmd/swarm issue cleanup --help
go run ./cmd/swarm storage report --help
```

CLI tests must cover `--include-storage` requiring `--all-merged`, preview default, `--apply`, `--json`, rejection with issue number/recovery/fork and worker apply, and upstream operator authorization for both backends. Report remains read-only and rejects apply. Verify invalid arguments cannot create control storage or acquire reservations.

Before creating the fragment in a checkout with approved Git objects, check `git cat-file -e '<approved-base-sha>:changes/unreleased/403.md'`. A successful check means modify existing; confirmed path absence means create. Missing commit/object is not proof of absence. Check current fragment format in `changes/unreleased/402.md`. Review changed documentation links, anchors, examples and parse any changed shell blocks with `bash -n`; verify example flags against actual help.

Record commands, commit/source identity when available, results and meaningful skips. The known main CLI replan-cap failure is outside these focused patterns; if a broader coordinator run encounters it, identify it separately without editing or hiding it.

## Tester-owned independent review

Read the WorkUnit and final code independently of planner assertions. Trace deletion from Cobra authorization through trusted-root/class admission, authoritative retention, use exclusion and root-bound recursive removal. Examine race windows inside traversal and between inspection and deletion; verify no metadata path becomes deletion authority and no lock/control record is removed. Verify all four acceptance rows against actual fixtures, including negative/partial results and the unchanged merged-task path. Audit producer sites to confirm that every allowed cache is reproducible and scratch retention protects unfinished recovery outputs.

Reuse applicable passing developer results after checking their source identity and coverage. Repeat commands only after relevant source changes, observed failures or unresolved coverage concerns; add a narrowly targeted adversarial case where review finds a gap. Strong independent review is required even when all commands pass. Observations remain advisory, not plan approval or claim-bound validation.

## Coordinator-owned reference policy and PR checklist

The coordinator runs the complete trusted-base required policy once after roles finish. The compiled policy is a reference, not a developer/tester checklist. Coordinator alone performs claim-bound validation, staging/publication and credentials handling. Follow the human plan gate; agents cannot approve it.

PR review checklist for environments unavailable here:

- Compare design to parent #378 sections A-D; reconcile against this authoritative WorkUnit.
- Verify the fragment's existence/absence at the approved base using available Git objects.
- Run the focused filesystem/exclusion/accounting tests on macOS, including trusted OS temp aliases, symlink refusal and sparse/hardlink semantics; use fixture coverage for platform-dependent calculations on Linux meanwhile.
- Exercise operator preview/apply on disposable local and GitHub-backed repositories if live backend qualification is desired; fixtures cover both backend decisions inside the sandbox. No live service or macOS access is a prerequisite to implementing the verifiable portion.

No OCI runtime qualification, remote archival, broad harness checks or authenticated model calls are added to this WorkUnit.
